http://www.bozemandailychronicle.com/new.text: INSTAGRAM FACEBOOK On July 6, the Sanders County Sheriff’s Office in western Montana put up a rather odd post on Facebook. It was a picture of a deputy standing with a smiling woman outside the sheriff’s office. “Good afternoon, Sanders County residents,” the post read. “We have met and spoken with Sinija Loze. She works with Families for Education. She is a college student from Latvia doing her summer job selling educational products by Southwestern Advantage. We have verified her information, she does have a accent but is a very nice lady. Her vehicle is a Grey jeep. No need to be alarmed if you see her.” The post got hundreds of reactions on Facebook, and many commenters were either confused or angry. In a since-deleted post on Facebook, the Sanders County Sheriff's Office wrote what a door-to-door salesperson asked them to write. Facebook “I’m genuinely confused about the purpose of this post?” one of the top comments read. “Are people in Montana ‘alarmed’ by someone with an ‘accent’? Literally everybody has an accent.” Someone else wondered if it was the “accent” part or the “selling educational products” that had everyone “on edge.” Many comments were either xenophobic or assailing the sheriff’s office for implying that people with accents were to be feared unless told otherwise. The odd part, however, is that the woman had presented the Sanders County Sheriff’s Office with a script, basically, of what to write. And she’s given it to other sheriff’s offices in Montana, who have also obliged her. By July 11, the original post from Sanders County had been deleted. The Sanders County Sheriff’s Office then posted a response. The post from Sweet Grass County. Facebook “Earlier this week, a young woman who is working in Sanders County as a door-to-door salesperson came in to the Sanders County Sheriff’s Office voluntarily to introduce herself, present her credentials and help prevent any confusion or unnecessary concern while she was working in the area,” the post read. The post went on to say that deputies had “determined that she is legitimately conducting business in our country.” “The intent of the post was never to stereotype, demean or judge her based on her nationality, ethnicity or accent,” the second statement read. “It was intended to support her request ... and reassure residents who had contacted our office with concerns. Unfortunately, the attention surrounding the post has had a very real effect on the young woman involved. She returned to our office today in tears after experiencing hostile interactions while working, including people yelling at her and aggressively telling her to leave.” The post went on to say “disagreement with door-to-door sales does not justify treating another person with hostility or cruelty.” “We recognize that the wording of the original post was interpreted differently than intended,” the statement continued. “For that reason, the original post has been removed. We hope this clarification provides the full context and reminds everyone that there is a real person at the center of this situation who deserves to be treated with basic courtesy and respect.” In an email to the Missoulian, Sanders County Sheriff Shawn Fielders said that the woman presented the phrasing. “The post we put up per her request was the exact same post that Sweet Grass County posted for her,” he explained. “She actually supplied a copy of their post for us to use. That included the part about the accent, she does have a very strong accent and is at times hard to understand so she requested we leave that in the post.” The post from the Laurel Police Department. Facebook Also, the Carbon County Sheriff’s Office posted the exact same wording on June 15, including the part about the accent. The Gallatin County Sheriff’s Office made a similar post, noting the color and model of the students’ cars, but didn’t mention the accent. The Laurel Police Department also posted a similar statement about a different woman from Latvia, using nearly the same language. The woman was also selling educational materials, like study guides for the ACT. “Lilija is driving a white Dodge and has an accent, please do not be intimidated by that,” the Laurel post reads. “If you are not in interested, she will thank you for your time and leave you in a good mood.” Of course, there were plenty of comments on that one too. Some questioned why the post was necessary. The post from Gallatin County. The Belgrade News profiled a young student in 2023, writing that the company recruits workers in Latvia .{/div}{/div}{/div}{/div}{/div}{/div}{/div} Valley Neighbors of the Flathead, a nonprofit that works to support immigrants in the Kalispell area, chimed in about the Sanders County post. “When Valley Neighbors works to make the Flathead or our region a more welcoming place for immigrants, we sometimes get pushback from folks who take issue with the idea that our communities actively grapple with xenophobia and racism,” the organization wrote on social media. “Earlier this week, the Sanders County Sheriff’s Office made a pre-emptive post about a young Latvian woman who would be going door-to-door as a salesperson. While we certainly can defer to the Sheriff’s Office about their intent, the language they used likely fell short in tone and intention. In (the post) you’ll likely see a lot of cringe xenophobic comments expressed in the comments thread. This incident, in a variety of ways, shows how far Montana has to go.” David Erickson is the business reporter for the Missoulian. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/08/magy.text: Menü Kereső Hatalmas a csomagtorlódás a Magyar Posta logisztikai központjában, a vállalat technológiai átállásra hivatkozik Belföld Nádor András Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Hatalmas a csomagtorlódás, leállásközeli állapotok vannak a Magyar Posta ecseri logisztikai központjában, nem csak átmeneti problémák vannak a csomagszállítással – számolt be a HVG-nek egy, a Postát belülről ismerő forrás. Azt mondta, a csomagok több mint két hete a szokásos 1-2 nap helyett 3-6 nap alatt érkeznek meg, de elmondása szerint már 2 hetes kézbesítésekről is beszámolnak a postai dolgozók. A Magyar Posta a lap megkeresésére arról írt, technológiai átállás miatt „átmenetileg meghosszabbodhat a csomagok kézbesítése”. „A korszerű szortírozó rendszerek finomhangolása és az informatikai rendszerek integrációja, az új helyszín beüzemelése során problémák léptek fel, amelyek közvetlenül érinthetik a csomagok feldolgozási idejét” – írta a Posta egy korábbi közleményben. Azt ígérték, mindent megtesznek annak érdekében, hogy a logisztikai folyamatok a lehető leggyorsabban visszaálljanak a normál üzletmenetbe. A HVG forrásai szerint viszont nem csak kisebb fennakadások vannak a csomagszállításban, nagyobb lehet a baj. Egy olvasójuk arra panaszkodott, hogy Debrecenből rendelt augusztus közepén egy levél méretű csomagot, benne egyetlen alkatrésszel. A Posta nyomkövetője szerint nyolc napig csak állt a debreceni központban, majd miután váratlanul Budapestre ért, az ügyfél kapott egy levelet, hogy van egy napja átvenni a csomagot az automatából, különben visszaküldik a feladónak. Vasárnap a Telexen is megjelent egy cikk, amiben arról írtunk, András milyen kálvárián ment keresztül , amikor a Magyar Posta csomagszállító vállalata, az MPL vitte házhoz a Bauhaus webshopjában vásárolt radiátorát. A HVG szerint a postai dolgozók részére fenntartott zárt Facebook-csoportban rengetegen panaszkodnak. Többen a megnövekedett munkaterhelésre, mások csak az elakadt csomagjukat akarják megkapni. A lap arról írt, akár 100 ezer csomag is feltorlódhatott országosan, nagy részük Ecseren áll. A probléma súlyát jelzi, hogy vidéki, kevésbé leterhelt régiókból szállítanak fel postai dolgozókat a Pest megyei településre, miközben a vállalat nem tájékoztatja megfelelően a dolgozókat. https://www.merimbulanewsweekly.com.au/s.text: An inquest into the deaths of three British aid workers killed by an Israeli drone strike in the Gaza Strip could be expanded to involve the family of the Australian colleague who died alongside them. Seven World Central Kitchen workers were killed when a three-car convoy was hit on April 1, 2024. An inquest in the UK will investigate the deaths of British citizens James Kirby, 47, John Chapman, 57 and James Henderson. Australian Lalzawmi "Zomi" Frankcom, 43, also died, with dual American-Canadian citizen Jacob Flickinger, 33, Polish national Damian Sobol, 35; and their driver, Palestinian Saifeddin Issam Ayad Abutaha, 25. The scope of inquests into the deaths of three British is set to be expanded to include the Israel Defence Forces and the commander who allegedly ordered the attack. During a pre-inquest hearing at Avon Coroner's Court on Monday, senior coroner Maria Voisin considered the scope of the full inquest and submissions by legal teams. Alison Hewitt, counsel to the inquest, said submissions had been made to grant interested person status - giving the right to participation during the proceedings - to the IDF and Colonel Nochi Mendel. "It is right to say that as part of the background facts, there has been a recognition that the deaths resulted from strikes ordered by or on behalf of Israeli Defence Forces and, it is said, specifically by Colonel Mendel," Hewitt said. Hewitt asked Voisin if it was correct that she was "minded to grant" interested person status to the IDF and Colonel Mendel, with the coroner replying "yes". Voisin also said she was likely to grant the status to the family of Frankcom and would confirm her position in writing in the near future. Granting interested person status gives an individual or organisation formal recognition and legal rights to participate in a coroner's investigation and hearing, meaning they can take part, see the evidence, give their own account and be represented by a lawyer. Hewitt said the scope inquest would include the circumstances by which the British workers came to be in Gaza, and what risk assessments, plans, policies and procedures were in place. Legal teams have proposed that be extended to cover the steps taken by the IDF and Israeli Ministry of Defence to protect the lives of humanitarian aid workers in Gaza. It should also consider how the IDF and World Community Kitchen worked together, and what information the IDF received prior to the strikes about the WCK's operations on April 1 An interview by ABC News with Colonel Mendel, including unedited recordings or transcripts, could also be requested. Australian Associated Press
